article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: White Widow × AK-47 × Blueberry
Breeder: Brothers In Farms
THC Content: 23–30%
CBD Content: 0.01–0.1%
Terpene Profile: Beta-caryophyllene , linalool , limonene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, earthy herbs, citrus, pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Hypothermia has a name that suggests numbness and immobility, but the experience is considerably more dynamic than that image implies. The first portion of the high can be bright, euphoric, and surprisingly energetic before an unmistakable physical calm begins creeping into the background. Its aroma follows a similarly contrasting path. Blueberry sweetness and citrus appear over damp earth, pine, peppery herbs, and diesel, creating a profile that feels rooted in an earlier generation of marijuana strains rather than the cake-and-candy genetics dominating many contemporary menus.

The version most widely documented under the Hypothermia name combines White Widow, AK-47, and Blueberry and is commonly attributed to Brothers In Farms. Current commercial flower demonstrates that these classic genetics can still deliver modern potency: recent Massachusetts products carrying the Hypothermia #1 name have appeared around 28–32% THC.
Genetics and Lineage

The best-established lineage for the Brothers In Farms version is White Widow × AK-47 × Blueberry. Contemporary commercial listings continue to identify that three-way pedigree, including 2026 Hypothermia #1 flower sold in Massachusetts. Each parent represents an influential branch of older cannabis breeding . White Widow contributes heavy resin coverage, earthy spice, and a balanced mental-and-physical character. AK-47 adds pungency, cerebral energy, and vigorous hybrid traits, while Blueberry brings sweeter berry aromatics, colorful flower tendencies, and a softer relaxing influence. Rather than relying on the modern Cookies or Gelato families , this cultivar draws much of its personality from strains that became famous decades earlier.

The name requires an important qualification. A second, genetically unrelated Hypothermia is currently documented as Blunicorn × Slurricane #23. PurLife’s own strain vault identifies its Hypothermia with that pedigree and describes it as a balanced hybrid featuring sweet, woodsy, and floral characteristics. Because both genetic versions circulate commercially, the breeder or producer should be checked before assuming that every jar labeled Hypothermia contains White Widow, AK-47, and Blueberry. This page focuses on the Brothers In Farms-associated triple cross, which remains the lineage most broadly attached to the name.
Effects and Experience

The onset can be surprisingly upbeat. A moderate dose often brings an elevated mood, easier conversation, and a mildly energetic mental state that may encourage creativity or make entertainment more absorbing. Rather than rushing immediately into sedation, the high tends to establish itself in the head first. Some consumers experience a playful or giggly quality, while others find the initial phase focused enough for music, gaming, casual projects, or social situations. That energetic opening reflects the AK-47 and White Widow sides of the family more clearly than the strain’s chilly name would suggest.

Physical relaxation gradually alters the experience. Muscles loosen, mental urgency fades, and the energetic edge becomes smoother as the body high gains strength. With enough marijuana, that transition can move all the way toward couch-lock or sleepiness. This progression makes dosage particularly important because commercially cultivated examples can be substantially stronger than older descriptions suggest. Hypothermia #1 flower has recently appeared at 28.31% THCA with 30.45% total active cannabinoids, while another commercial batch was listed at 32.11% THC. At those concentrations, inexperienced consumers may encounter dizziness, dry mouth, impaired concentration, or anxiety if they consume too much too quickly.
Medical Benefits

The gradual movement from mental uplift into physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer a cultivar capable of covering more than one part of the day. Smaller amounts may feel mentally lighter and less sedating, while larger servings can produce stronger body comfort and a quieter state. Consumers sometimes seek this type of effect profile when dealing with everyday stress, poor appetite, tension, low mood, or difficulty relaxing after an active day.

That does not establish Hypothermia as a treatment for any particular disease or symptom. Cannabis flower is chemically variable, and this strain is especially complicated because two unrelated genetic versions use the same name. THC levels also vary dramatically between batches. Medical consumers should base decisions on actual laboratory results, personal tolerance, route of administration, other medications, and appropriate healthcare guidance rather than assuming a strain name predicts a specific therapeutic outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Hypothermia’s aroma carries unmistakable traces of its older genetic foundation. Berry sweetness can appear immediately, particularly in examples expressing the Blueberry side strongly, but it rarely remains alone. Earthy herbs, pine needles, cracked pepper, citrus peel, and diesel add progressively sharper layers after the buds are broken apart. Some flower develops a chemical or almost metallic edge underneath the fruit, giving the scent a darker quality than a straightforward blueberry weed strain.

Beta-caryophyllene, linalool, and limonene are repeatedly associated with the White Widow × AK-47 × Blueberry version. Caryophyllene contributes pepper and dry spice, while limonene can sharpen the citrus element. Linalool adds a softer floral quality that sits between the berry sweetness and more pungent herbal notes. Individual laboratory profiles can also contain pinene and myrcene, which would reinforce the forest-like, earthy side of the aroma. Because terpene expression changes according to phenotype, environment, harvest timing, drying, and storage, no single terpene ratio should be treated as permanent.

On the palate, berry and citrus often lead the inhale before earth and herbs emerge. The exhale can become markedly more savory, carrying pepper, wood, pine, and diesel. That progression distinguishes Hypothermia from modern candy strains whose sweetness remains dominant from beginning to end. Its flavor has more of an old-school hybrid quality—fruit is present, but resinous earth and spice remain equally important.
Growing Information

Detailed cultivation specifications for the original Brothers In Farms release are difficult to verify, and there is no currently accessible breeder sheet establishing an official flowering period or yield. An indoor estimate of roughly eight to ten weeks is reasonable for the genetic family, but growers should treat that range as practical guidance rather than a breeder guarantee. This distinction matters because cultivation information published for the separate Blunicorn × Slurricane #23 Hypothermia cannot automatically be applied to the White Widow × AK-47 × Blueberry version.

The triple-cross lineage suggests a plant with enough hybrid vigor to respond well to topping, low-stress training, or trellising. White Widow and AK-47 ancestry can contribute substantial resin and productive branching, while Blueberry influence may bring denser flowers and greater color variation in some phenotypes. Creating an even canopy before flowering helps manage stretch and distributes light more effectively among multiple tops. Once flower density increases, interior airflow becomes increasingly important.

Outdoor growers should favor locations that provide strong sunlight and relatively dry weather through the autumn finish. A practical October harvest window is likely in many Northern Hemisphere climates, although latitude and phenotype can shift maturity in either direction. Final yield is better described as moderate to high than given a precise grams-per-plant figure without breeder documentation. Root space, sunlight, plant training, vegetative time, nutrition, and seasonal weather will ultimately determine production.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Hypothermia?

The widely documented Brothers In Farms version combines White Widow, AK-47, and Blueberry. Current commercial Hypothermia #1 flower continues to be sold under that three-way genetic description. A separate Hypothermia made from Blunicorn × Slurricane #23 also exists, so identifying the producer is important.
Is Hypothermia indica or sativa?

The White Widow × AK-47 × Blueberry cultivar is generally considered a balanced hybrid, although the later portion of the high can feel distinctly indica-like. Mental energy and euphoria tend to appear first, followed by increasingly noticeable physical relaxation.
How strong is Hypothermia?

Modern examples can be very potent. Commercial flower has appeared around 26–30% THC, while certain Hypothermia #1 batches have exceeded 30%. One Massachusetts offering was listed at 32.11% THC and 35.76% total active cannabinoids.
What does Hypothermia taste like?

Expect blueberry and berry sweetness mixed with citrus, earthy herbs, pine, pepper, wood, and diesel. Phenotypes leaning toward Blueberry may taste fruitier, while others emphasize the pungent and herbal character inherited from White Widow and AK-47.
Are there two different Hypothermia strains?

Yes. In addition to the White Widow × AK-47 × Blueberry cultivar commonly attributed to Brothers In Farms, another commercial Hypothermia is documented as Blunicorn × Slurricane #23. PurLife currently identifies its own Hypothermia with the latter lineage. The two should be treated as separate cultivars despite sharing a name.
Final Thoughts on Hypothermia

Hypothermia stands apart from much of today’s marijuana market because its better-known genetic version reaches back to White Widow, AK-47, and Blueberry rather than the endless succession of Gelato, Runtz, and Cookies crosses. Those parents give the cultivar a combination of berry sweetness, citrus, pine, earth, spice, and diesel that feels distinctly different from contemporary dessert weed. The effects show similar range, beginning with mental energy and euphoria before gradually cooling into stronger physical relaxation.

Its genetic ambiguity deserves equal attention. A Blunicorn × Slurricane #23 cultivar now circulates under the same Hypothermia name, meaning the label alone cannot establish what genetics are actually inside a package. For the Brothers In Farms-associated version covered here, the White Widow × AK-47 × Blueberry pedigree remains the central identifier. With modern batches capable of reaching roughly 30% THC or more, Hypothermia proves that a foundation built from classic cannabis genetics can still compete with today’s high-potency hybrids while delivering a flavor and effect profile that feels refreshingly removed from the modern candy-strain formula.
